assent.description: The parties' acts (§ 4.1.2). Each entry is written whole by the party its `role` implies. Entries MUST NOT be edited or removed

best_for.description: Advisory planning hints. Non-normative, and never the basis for a match

brief_id.description: The buyer's brief this proposal answers

buyer.description: The entity that assents, usually the agency. Its presence makes the proposal issued to that buyer (§ 4.3). Whom the spend is for is `commitment.advertisers[]` (§ 5.6.1), and whether the buyer may bind that advertiser is authorization (§ 1.2). `legal_name` is REQUIRED here

change_requests.description: Ordered post-`agreed` history. Each entry carries the fields of the OpenDirect 2.1 ChangeRequest, except its `webhook`, plus `baseline`, `actor`, `at`, and `cancellation`. Outside the binding record (§ 4.1.1) and the offered terms (§ 4.1.3), like `negotiation_history[]`, so an entry changes neither `record_digest` nor `version`

description.description: Prose, not a name. Where the "why buy" case is made, including which channels a multi-channel proposal spans

issued_from.description: The shared proposal and version an issued proposal was made from (§ 4.3). A pointer: nothing is inherited through it

line_items.description: The line items (§ 5), in the order the seller wrote them. A proposal holds `line_items[]` or `packages[]`, not both

negotiation_history.description: Ordered, append-only. Entries MUST NOT be edited or removed. A commit and its answers are in `assent[]`, not here, and an entry here voids nothing

offer_window.description: The window the offer holds: it does not hold before `start` or after `end`. This is the offer window, not the campaign flight

packages.description: The line items in packages (§ 4.1.4), in the order the seller wrote them

proposal_template_id.description: Links a proposal to the seller's template. Opaque to buyers; used for the seller's reporting

seller.description: The selling entity. `seller.domain` is the seller's identifier for all purposes, including `assent[]`. `legal_name` is REQUIRED here

spec_version.description: The version of this specification the document follows, such as `3.0`

version.description: Monotonically increasing revision number, starting at 1, held by the seller. Each version is a snapshot of the proposal's offered terms (§ 4.1.3). A version is frozen at the earliest of: the proposal's `status` leaving `draft`; a `negotiation_history[]` or `assent[]` entry naming it; a counterparty receiving it in any representation (§ 2.1). The offered terms of a frozen version MUST NOT change; a change to them creates version `n+1`. The values § 4.1.3 lists as not offered terms change without a new version
